task: Classify mice by genotype (control c or trisomic t, the Ts65Dn model of Down syndrome), learning protocol (context-shock CS or shock-context SC) and treatment (memantine m or saline s) from protein expression in the cerebral cortex.
instructions: You are helping a feature-selection search for a classification task. Rate how useful each feature is likely to be for predicting the class, on its own or together with a few others, from 0 (useless) to 1 (most useful). Use only your knowledge of the domain and the descriptions given; you do not see the data. Reply with a JSON object only: {"scores": {"<feature index>": <score>, ...}} with one entry for every feature index listed.

calls.reply:
This is the Higuera et al. mouse protein expression dataset (Ts65Dn). I'm relying on recall of the published findings, not on the data.

Features that, as I recall, discriminate classes well:
- Genotype: DYRK1A, ITSN1, APP, SOD1, and also BRAF, pERK, and others, since these are overexpressed or altered in trisomic mice.
- Learning protocol: pCFOS, ARC, EGR1, pCREB, and others.
- Treatment: BAD, pCASP9, and others.

In this dataset, top-ranked features commonly include:
- Selected by SOM and ranking: DYRK1A, ITSN1, pERK, pCAMKII, BRAF, APP, SOD1, pPKCG, pNR2A, pJNK, Tau, pMEK, NR2A, pELK, AcetylH3K9, CaNA, GluR3, GluR4, Ubiquitin, SHH, BAD, BCL2, pS6, H3AcK18, pGSK3B, nNOS, ARC, and others.
- The published 3-protein subsets included SOD1, pERK, DYRK1A, ITSN1, BRAF, pCAMKII, pNR2A, and others.

I scored these by recall and plausibility, with higher values for the features above.
